question: Which electrical component is used to perform a polarity test to check whether or not the switches are connected in phase/live cable?
solution:
The correct answer is __Test lamp**(Option 1)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Test lamp__ is a simple device used to check the presence of voltage in electrical circuits.
 
• It is commonly used to test whether switches are connected to the live or phase wire in the circuit.
 
• A test lamp works by completing a circuit, causing the lamp to illuminate when it detects voltage.
 
• It is a reliable tool for polarity testing and identifying live wires.
 
• Test lamps are widely used due to their simplicity and ease of operation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Ammeter:**
 
 
• An ammeter is used to measure the current flowing through a circuit.
 
• It is not suitable for polarity testing as it does not detect live wires.
 
 
 
• **Multimeter:**
 
 
• A multimeter is a versatile tool used to measure voltage, current, and resistance.
 
• While it can test polarity, it is more complex compared to a test lamp for this purpose.
 
 
 
• **Megger:**
 
 
• A megger is used to measure insulation resistance in electrical installations.
 
• It is not designed for polarity testing.
